transcript.text: Just had a new induction hob fitted, Beko. When I put my saucepan on it just flashes a U and doesn't heat. Is it faulty? It's brand new!!

A flashing 'U' on a Beko induction hob almost always means it cannot detect a suitable pan. It is rarely a fault with the appliance itself, especially when brand new. Induction hobs only heat magnetic cookware (cast iron or certain stainless steels). If the pan is aluminium, copper, or has a warped base, the hob will flash 'U' and not heat. 1. Does it hold firmly? If not, that pan will not work on any induction zone.
Try placing that same saucepan on a different heating zone. Does it still flash 'U', or does it heat up? If the magnet sticks but the pan still flashes 'U' on every zone, let me know - we can check if the child lock is engaged.
I tried a fridge magnet and it doesn't stick to the saucepans! I haven't tried them on a different zone yet. What does that mean, are they no good?

That suggests the saucepans are not suitable for induction cooking. Induction hobs only work with magnetic pans; if a fridge magnet doesn't stick to the base, that pan will never heat up on an induction hob and the 'U' code is normal behaviour. You have two options:
1. Buy new induction-compatible saucepans (look for a spiral symbol on the base or check the packaging).
2. If you need to use these existing pans immediately, you would need a separate conventional electric hotplate or gas hob, as they won't work with this Beko unit. Since the hob is brand new and working correctly by detecting that the pan is unsuitable, there is no fault with the appliance itself.
